newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council to mull fund to boost European film sector.
newsitem.headline: Council to mull fund to boost European film sector.

text.p: The Culture Council meets on Monday to consider an investment plan for the continent's film industry, having abandoned plans to restrict Hollywood imports.
The plan, which Europe's film-makers say could help create two million jobs over the next 10 years, faces a tough ride.

The European Commission has begged EU governments to set up a 90 million Ecu loan guarantee fund, saying it would last 17 years and generate enough capital to finance 415 films and 215 television productions.
The fund -- which would be managed by the European Investment Fund -- would encourage financial institutions to invest in film production by guaranteeing a proportion of the loans they make.
To overcome German-led resistance, Ireland, which holds the EU's presidency, is expected to propose slashing the planned budget by a third to 60 million Ecus.

Hollywood is able to cover production costs in its enormous monolingual domestic market and then sell its films and television programmes in Europe at a tenth of the price it would cost Europeans to make something similar.

The diversity of languages makes distribution difficult in the 15-nation European market. As a result eight out of 10 films shown in the cinema and six out of 10 shown on television in Europe are from the United States.

Resistance from member states forced the European Parliament last month to finally drop long-standing demands for mandatory limits on the number of Hollywood films and television programmes on European television.

Europe's major filmmakers -- grouped in the European Film Companies Alliance -- say they prefer the help offered by the guarantee fund plan, which they say will encourage them to make relatively risky large-scale investments in European films.
"We believe that Europe can help the film industry better maybe in a different manner than has always been the case," said Philippe Kern, director of European affairs for PolyGram.

"The European Film Companies Alliance believes the Audivisual Guarantee Fund would boost Europe's flagging film industry...The Audiovisual Guarantee Fund would be a very effective tool for promoting the cinema industry in the European Union," the alliance said.
